items.summary: TRUSTWORTHY AUTONOMOUS BIOLABORATORIES THROUGH MICROROBOTICS AND QUANTUM SENSING AT THE LIMIT Replayable Experiments x Permission Governance x External Metrology STARLI Research Institute XXIX - Flagship Research Monograph 20 Can an autonomous biolaboratory become scientifically useful without acquiring the authority to redefine its own permissions, validate its own evidence, or release untraceable measurements? This nonclinical research monograph investigates a bounded laboratory architecture connecting microrobotic sample handling, quantum-enabled and classical sensing, independent metrological reference chains, experiment replay, physical safe stopping, and human authority. Its central proposition is that reliable autonomy is a property of the entire evidence pathway rather than of any single robotic manipulator or AI model. A laboratory result is eligible for release only when sample identity and integrity, authorized execution, traceable references, justified uncertainty limits, and external acceptance are all demonstrated. An apparently successful action is not equivalent to a scientifically accepted sample. Digital replay does not replace physical replication, cryptographic event integrity does not guarantee sensor truth, and a quantum hardware label does not establish a practical sensing advantage. The research design is developed across 82 chapter-level inquiries with five independently paginated investigations per chapter, 30 connected mathematical research plates, 200 distinct Research Gates, and 33 Phoenix Answer Embryos. The chapters address typed authority graphs, specimen provenance, sample exposure, closed-chip physics, covariance-aware sensing, AI planning within finite action spaces, common-cause fault injection, external interlocks, blinded classical benchmarks, evidence DAGs, cross-site replication, data retention, and responsible system retirement. The proposed minimum experimental prototype uses a closed microfluidic chip with interchangeable handling modules, two independently referenced readout channels, simulated or inert-tracer specimens, a separate audit service, and a physically verifiable stop mechanism. Proposed tests include unauthorized-action challenges, hidden calibration drift, interrupted events, sample contamination, unannounced network partitions, and independent laboratory replay or rerun. DOI-linked scientific references establish the relevant literature in automated laboratories, microrobotics, quantum sensing, uncertainty metrology, FAIR data stewardship, and computational reproducibility. They do not independently validate the integrated system proposed here. SCIENTIFIC STATUS AND LIMITATIONS This book is a hypothesis-forming nonclinical research architecture. It reports no completed microrobotic or quantum biosensing experiments, no demonstrated clinical performance, no universal quantum advantage, and no autonomous system capable of authorizing itself. Statistical models, formulas, and decision policies require experimental verification, specialized review, and appropriate boundary conditions. A failed external reference, unavailable provenance chain, or revoked permission requires abstention rather than inference by convenience. STARLI RESEARCH PHILOSOPHY A trustworthy laboratory must remain answerable to evidence outside itself. Autonomy becomes scientifically meaningful when an experiment can be stopped, questioned, reconstructed, and handed to future researchers who retain the right to refuse its original assumptions.

items.summary: This archive provides the computational methods, structural coordinate files, source data, model outputs, and reproducibility documentation supporting an exploratory investigation of geometric persistence and prediction uncertainty at HIV-1 envelope (Env) glycan sites. The research examines whether local sequence divergence and sparse structural-context observations can improve the identification of unreliable glycan-site geometric predictions. The approach combines sequence-informed error estimation with residual information obtained from six observed glycan-site probes. Held-out evaluations included five BG505-derived Env structures and two JR-FL structures. In the original experiments, the six-probe method improved pooled dangerous-error discrimination relative to sequence-only prediction, with ROC AUC increasing from 0.704 to 0.945 in BG505 and from 0.522 to 0.761 in JR-FL. These results are exploratory. The original evaluations contained only two dangerous underestimates in BG505 and three in JR-FL. Within-structure discrimination did not consistently improve, and training-test construct overlap was identified. Additional construct-family exclusion analyses document the sensitivity of the findings to training composition and failure prevalence. The principal computational outputs were regenerated exactly from archived structural coordinates using the supplied scripts. The archive includes frozen protocols, structural data, prediction tables, provenance audits, family-exclusion analyses, and a companion manuscript draft. The study supports further investigation of sparse structural context for uncertainty assessment but does not establish reliable cross-strain site-level failure detection, glycan occupancy prediction, or protein synthesis prediction. This deposit is intended to support transparency, independent reproduction, methodological evaluation, and future extension of HIV-1 Env structural bioinformatics research. This research extends the author's previously deposited HIV-1 Env glycan-shield investigations by examining the predictive and uncertainty-assessment implications of geometric persistence, local structural constraints, and glycan-site organization.
items.title: Ensemble Geometric Persistence: HIV-1 Env Glycan-Site Geometry and Sparse Structural-Context Uncertainty Assessment (Reproducibility Archive)

items.summary: This Zenodo record accompanies the paper “Scalable Measurement-Based Quantum Simulation Patterns for Benchmarking” arXiv.2605.12502   and provides QPatLib v1.0 measurement-pattern datasets in human-readable JSONL together with a ZIP archive of OpenQASM 3.0 circuits used for validation and reproducibility.  The patterns and circuits implement Pauli string unitaries  for benchmark cases.  Cases include all possible string combinations for less than 6 qubits and strings used in Hamiltonians for certain diatomic molecules for 6 or more qubits.     Format:  Each  pattern_*.jsonl file is containins measurement patterns for all subsets for a given model/instance and subset strategy: it begins with a preamble containing model metadata, subset definitions, provenance, and (when feasible) full-pattern test results, followed by one pattern entry per subset. Each subset entry includes a required  pattern_ascii field storing the measurement pattern in the measurement-calculus/Graphix standard with signal shifting, written left-to-right in the canonical order nodes → edges → measurements (with signal dependencies) → byproduct corrections (X/Z). The circuits are included as circuit_files.zip.   Patterns in this record were validated against the corresponding circuits and checked for causal flow.   Codes for generating these patterns can be found at QPatLib repository on Github
items.title: QPatLib v1.0 — Measurement-based quantum simulation Pauli string unitary pattern collections

items.summary: NovaFabric is self-hosted, open-source replay and evidence infrastructure for AI agents and agentic systems. It captures agent executions as portable, secret-scanned Run Capsules and provides replay, behavioral and structural diff, lineage, cryptographic provenance, assurance, and audit around those executions. The same capture layer can wrap general commands and runs entirely in the user's own infrastructure, from local environments through Kubernetes to SLURM/HPC, with no accounts and no telemetry. It is built around five primitives — Asset Registry, Run Capsule, Replay, Lineage, and Evidence Bundle — and five explicit replay modes (forensic, mocked, semantic, exact, and the experimental intervention mode). Run Capsules can be sealed with the user’s own key; sealing is opt-in. Evidence bundles verify offline using only sha256sum and an ed25519 verifier, with no NovaFabric installation required. Interoperates with established specifications rather than inventing formats: OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions, in-toto/DSSE, RFC 3161 timestamping, W3C PROV, OpenLineage, and CycloneDX.
items.title: NovaFabric: replayable, verifiable execution evidence for AI agents

items.summary: Motivation: Variant calling for next-generation sequencing (NGS) data relies on a diverse ecosystem of tools and workflows. Large-scale collaborative studies increasingly adopt federated analysis, where each institution processes sensitive data locally using standardized pipelines. Deploying identical pipelines across multiple centers remains challenging because heterogeneous software environments and computing policies can cause workflow divergence and inconsistent results. Results: We developed CBIcall, a workflow backend-flexible, configuration-driven framework that runs standardized variant-calling pipelines from raw FASTQ files to analysis-ready VCFs. Users define each analysis in a single YAML parameters file, which CBIcall resolves against a controlled workflow registry and resource catalog. The execution driver validates parameters and checks compatibility among pipelines, analysis modes, workflow backends, genome builds, tool versions, and resource bundles. CBIcall supports reproducibility auditing by comparing executions using recorded provenance and output fingerprints. CBIcall dispatches validated workflows natively through Bash, Cromwell, Nextflow and Snakemake backends and provides production-ready pipelines for germline WES, WGS (single-sample or cohort joint genotyping following GATK Best Practices), and mitochondrial DNA analysis. We evaluated analytical performance using public benchmark datasets and validated reproducibility across four computing environments. We further deployed CBIcall in the EU HEREDITARY project, where it processed 1102 samples with both WES and mtDNA pipelines on an institutional HPC system, supporting its suitability for reproducible cohort-scale genomic analyses. Availability and implementation: CBIcall is open source (GPLv3) and distributed with ready-to-run pipelines; full dependency and installation documentation is available at https://github.com/CNAG-Biomedical-Informatics/cbicall.
items.title: CBIcall: a configuration-driven framework for variant calling in large sequencing cohorts

items.summary: This is a study commissioned by the Panel for the Future of Science and Technology, European Parliament: Generative Artificial Intelligence could strengthen open science by improving accessibility, findability, and usability. Still, under less favourable conditions, it could also weaken scientific exchange by obscuring provenance, deepening dependency on opaque infrastructures, and reinforcing inequalities and increasing synthetic overload, in which large volumes of AI-generated scientific content overwhelm the capacity of researchers and systems to verify, interpret, and trust information. This study describes how Generative AI is reshaping scientific exchange within the broader framework of open science. It shows that the main policy challenge is not whether Generative AI will be used in scientific exchange, but under what institutional, infrastructural, and normative conditions it can support reliable research, and knowledge valorisation. The European Union should treat scientific exchange as public-interest infrastructure and enact policies to support skills, strengthened provenance, transparency, reproducibility, inclusion, and strategic capacity in an AI-mediated research environment. This report provides specific policy options tackling the risks that can be associated with the use of AI in scientific exchange. This study is prepared for, and addressed to, the Members and staff of the European Parliament as background material to assist them in their parliamentary work. The content of the document is the sole responsibility of its author(s) and any opinions expressed herein should not be taken to represent an official position of the Parliament.
items.title: Open science and the effects of Generative Artificial Intelligence in scientific exchange: Policy options for reliable research

items.summary: Supplementary methods, results, data tables and analysis code for the manuscript Inflammatory and NRF2-associated transcriptional responses in human intracerebral hemorrhage: paired myeloid evidence and gene-set sensitivity. The five resources contain supplementary methods, tables and figures, detailed data workbooks, reproducibility code and supporting audit documentation. Original code is licensed under MIT; original documentation and derived content are licensed under CC BY 4.0. Third-party materials retain their source terms; see LICENSES.md and source notices inside Online_Resource_3.zip. Manuscript abstract Public intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) datasets cover different tissue compartments and measure different subsets of genes, complicating comparisons across studies. We compared four specified gene sets (inflammation, complement, microglial activation and nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2 (NRF2)-associated oxidative stress) in public paired human brain, single-cell and hematoma-effluent/blood datasets, using patients rather than cells as inferential units. In two studies of paired brain tissue, inflammation, complement and NRF2-associated scores were higher in perihematomal than contralateral samples in all four patient blocks and five matched pairs. Patient-level single-cell comparisons found higher inflammatory and complement scores in microglia/monocyte groups than in comparator lineages. In 14 patients with same-hour paired CD14+ and neutrophil data, a five-gene score named for microglial activation showed a positive CD14+–neutrophil local-response interaction in all 14 (adjusted P=0.000488), but four-program heterogeneity was not established (Friedman P=0.0796). Restricting this score to three shared genes reversed its CD14+ local response; a jointly scaled three-gene interaction was near zero. Independent acute blood data showed positive case-control differences, whereas longitudinal changes were not significant after adjustment. Inflammatory and NRF2-associated expression differences recurred across these datasets. The CD14+ local response of the microglial-related score depended on its measured genes. Version 2026-10-24 changes This revision aligns the five supplementary resources with the current manuscript and adds the exact GSE163256 primary fractional-count-to-score reconstruction and fresh-score downstream verification. Earlier domain-score displays in Online Resource 2, worksheets 05 and 06, are replaced by the fixed-program paired-brain results already used in the manuscript. Superseded, undocumented competitive-null fields are removed from the current Puy13 summary display and export; the defined manufacturer-panel-matched analysis is retained. Scoring and provenance descriptions, archive entry points, fonts, table formatting and numerical display precision have also been corrected. The primary biological scores and current inferential statistics are unchanged. Earlier inputs and execution records are retained with their historical roles identified.

items.summary: Overview This software package accompanies the study Resolvability of Ionospheric Currents From Multi-LEO Magnetometry . It provides computational tools for investigating how multi-altitude satellite magnetic observations constrain three-dimensional ionospheric currents. The package implements a divergence-free spherical Mie magnetic-field representation and a Bayesian inversion framework for evaluating magnetic-field and current reconstruction, degrees of freedom for signal (DFS), physical-current information, and posterior uncertainty. Main Features Spherical-harmonic Mie forward modeling and three-component current reconstruction. Bayesian inversion with full posterior covariance propagation. Resolution and recoverability diagnostics for different satellite configurations and observation altitudes. Physical-current information analysis and regularization-sensitivity experiments. Synthetic current-recovery experiments, calibration routines, and figure-generation workflows. Python and optional MATLAB implementations, with independent numerical verification. Sample Swarm-A/B orbital positions for geometry tests and a self-contained synthetic inversion example. What's New in This Version 3 This release provides a corrected scientific implementation and updated reproducibility tools. The principal corrections include: Correcting the colatitude derivative of the associated Legendre functions used in the spherical-harmonic operator. Restoring the radial magnetic-field contribution of the quadratic poloidal Mie term, ensuring consistency with the continuous divergence-free representation. Updating the corresponding current-reconstruction and recoverability calculations. Clarifying the scaled coefficient parameterization, Bayesian prior, and interpretation of coefficient-space resolution diagnostics. Improving numerical verification, reproducibility workflows, and documentation. The updated calculations continue to support the importance of satellite altitude separation for constraining specified ionospheric current structures, while distinguishing formal information gain from recovery of the complete physical current distribution. Data and Reproducibility The package includes source code, documentation, numerical tests, small reference summaries, sample orbit positions, and a self-contained synthetic example. The synthetic demonstrations can be executed without downloading mission magnetic-field observations. Reproducing the study's observation-based analyses requires the corresponding processed Swarm and Macau Science Satellite-1 data and additional external inputs described in the documentation. Large intermediate numerical archives and original magnetic observation records are not redistributed in this software package. Citation and License Please cite the version-specific Zenodo DOI and the software authors listed in CITATION.cff when using this package. Author-owned software and documentation are distributed under the MIT License. Included spacecraft-derived orbit excerpts and external datasets remain subject to their respective data-provider terms. This release supersedes the previous software implementation while retaining earlier versions in the same Zenodo version history.

items.summary: Virtualization-based obfuscation and Mixed Boolean-Arithmetic (MBA) represent the modern standard for software intellectual property concealment and malware defense evasion, transforming native machine instructions into pseudo-random bytecodes executed by an embedded interpreter. Existing deobfuscation paradigms remain fundamentally brittle: dynamic execution tracing achieves incomplete path coverage while triggering anti-analysis defenses; classical Dynamic Symbolic Execution (DSE) suffers from catastrophic path explosion and prohibitive SMT solver latency over modular bit-vector arithmetic; and virtual stack mechanics leave hundreds of dead operations that overwhelm industry decompilers. In this paper, we present AETHER-64, a fully automated, static bytecode-driven devirtualization and algebraic simplification framework engineered specifically for 64-bit protected binaries. AETHER-64 introduces three foundational innovations: (1) Local-Context Handler Symbolic Slicing, which reconstructs complete Control-Flow Graphs (CFGs) through isolated basic block emulation without accumulating global path constraints; (2) a bit-parallel Algebraic Pre-Reduction (APR) filter grounded in Boolean conjunction lattice signatures and fast Moebius inversion over Z/2^64, resolving invariant dispatch conditions in O(1) time; and (3) syntax-directed I/O-guided non-linear MBA synthesis coupled with LLVM Static Single Assignment (SSA) virtual stack elimination. We evaluate AETHER-64 on the Quarkslab Diffing Obfuscation Dataset (104 ground-truth functions across MiniLua, Zlib, and SQLite comprising 56,883 bytecode instructions), 1,000 synthetic Tigress virtual machines, commercial protections (VMProtect 3.4/3.5, Themida 3.1), and 7-layer non-linear MBA expressions. AETHER-64 achieves 100% CFG recovery, resolves 93.91% of branch queries via APR filtering with an empirical 2,072.8x speedup over raw SMT resolution, eliminates 91.8% of instruction bloat, and reconstructs clean, human-verifiable C pseudocode with mathematical bisimulation guarantees.
items.title: AETHER-64: High-Throughput Binary Devirtualization via Bit-Parallel Algebraic Pre-Reduction and SSA Bytecode Promotion

items.summary: USGS Groundwater-Depth Dataset Processing Workflow v1.0.0 is the archived software release of the public processing workflow developed to construct the Version 1.0 quality-controlled daily groundwater-depth dataset derived from the U.S. Geological Survey National Water Information System (USGS NWIS). The workflow processes USGS parameter 72019 (depth to water below land surface), daily mean statistic 00003, Approved source values, and wells classified with USGS code U (Unconfined single aquifer). It implements normalization and quality control, temporal continuity assessment, segmentation of fragmented monitoring histories, development and reserved-validation masking, PCHIP reconstruction of short internal gaps, and final dataset export with explicit source/interpolation provenance. The frozen workflow uses a minimum retained span of 10 years, a maximum internal missing-gap threshold of 30 days, PCHIP interpolation without extrapolation, exactly 50 development masks and 20 reserved-validation masks per required gap length where applicable, and a pooled RMSE acceptance threshold of 0.20 m at every required masking length. Segment selection is fixed before reserved validation, and no alternative segment is substituted after a reserved-validation failure. The software supported construction of a final dataset containing 331 monitoring wells and 2,374,112 daily values, including 2,357,801 retained USGS source values and 16,311 PCHIP-reconstructed values. The associated scientific dataset is archived separately on Zenodo and is not distributed as part of this software record. This repository is a public adaptation of the research workflow with portable paths and reproducibility documentation. The scientific processing criteria and numerical methods of the frozen Version 1.0 workflow are preserved. Source repository: https://github.com/joelgarciapazos/usgs-groundwater-processing Release: v1.0.0

items.summary: QUANTUM SENSING AND MICROROBOTIC PERTURBATION ANALYSIS OF CELLULAR MICROENVIRONMENTS AT THE LIMIT Microenvironment Gradients × Quantum Readout × Measurement-Induced Perturbation Separation STARLI Research Institute XXIX — Flagship Research Monograph 13 What happens when an instrument changes the very microenvironment it is supposed to measure? This research monograph investigates the scientific and engineering boundaries of quantum-enabled thermometry and microrobotic observation in confined, nonclinical cellular microenvironment models. Its central question is whether a localized temperature or magnetic-field gradient can be separated from disturbances introduced by the sensing and manipulation apparatus itself. The proposed research architecture combines hydrogel phantoms, controlled heat sources, nitrogen-vacancy (NV) diamond sensors, independent classical fluorescent thermometry, spatial reference points, blinded sham-actuation experiments, and uncertainty-aware thermal-field reconstruction. Rather than treating a sharp image or improved instrument sensitivity as proof of biological discovery, the study asks how to establish the physical origin, spatial validity, and reproducibility of each reported field. The 770-page volume contains 82 research chapters, five independently paginated research sections per chapter, 30 interconnected mathematical derivation plates, 200 Research Gates, and 33 Phoenix Answer Embryos. Topics range from NV resonance cross-sensitivity, microwave and laser heating, photon statistics, soft-matter interfaces, hydrodynamic motion, and anisotropic thermal conduction to causal controls, inverse problems, spatial covariance, interlaboratory comparison, and qualified instrument retirement. Each research chapter connects a physical mechanism to a falsifiable claim, a nonclinical experimental comparator, a measurement endpoint, and an explicit condition for withholding or retiring the conclusion. The Research Gates preserve actionable questions for future investigators. The Phoenix Answer Embryos offer provisional designs that can be separated, reconfigured, or abandoned when evidence contradicts them. DOI-linked scholarly literature supplies foundations for metrology, quantum sensing, microhandling, and thermal-field measurement without being mistaken for validation of the proposed integrated platform. Scientific Scope and Limitations This is a hypothesis-forming research blueprint, not a report of completed laboratory experiments or independently peer-reviewed findings. It does not establish autonomous nanoscale robotic systems, clinical diagnostic performance, therapeutic efficacy, or universal quantum advantage. Its minimum experimental setting uses confined hydrogels, artificial microenvironments, and properly authorized reference materials. A temperature or magnetic-field reading alone cannot establish cell health, metabolism, viability, or treatment outcomes. STARLI Research Philosophy A scientifically responsible observation includes the possibility that observing changed the result. By making such failures measurable, preserving negative evidence, and leaving research questions open to revision, this monograph invites future human and AI researchers to challenge, extend, and reconstruct its proposed methods.

Existing approaches address these limitations primarily through additional architectural components, leaving optimization-level intervention comparatively underexplored. We introduce a constraint-aware optimization framework combining Balanced Mean Squared Error, a Siamese anti-symmetric regularizer, and a novel OOD-margin consistency loss on the per-position feature representation, requiring no architectural changes to the SPURS backbone. Across eleven benchmarks and three random seeds, the framework improves Spearman correlation on S669 from 0.486 to 0.540 ($σ=0.002$ across seeds), matching the published SPURS baseline (0.50) without architectural modification, and on S461 from 0.653 to 0.711, with consistent smaller gains on five additional OOD datasets. items.summary: Overview This software package accompanies the study Resolvability of Ionospheric Currents From Multi-LEO Magnetometry . It provides computational tools for investigating how multi-altitude satellite magnetic observations constrain three-dimensional ionospheric currents. The package implements a divergence-free spherical Mie magnetic-field representation and a Bayesian inversion framework for evaluating magnetic-field and current reconstruction, degrees of freedom for signal (DFS), physical-current information, and posterior uncertainty. Main Features Spherical-harmonic Mie forward modeling and three-component current reconstruction. Bayesian inversion with full posterior covariance propagation. Resolution and recoverability diagnostics for different satellite configurations and observation altitudes. Physical-current information analysis and regularization-sensitivity experiments. Synthetic current-recovery experiments, calibration routines, and figure-generation workflows. Python and optional MATLAB implementations, with independent numerical verification. Sample Swarm-A/B orbital positions for geometry tests and a self-contained synthetic inversion example. What's New in This Version 3 This release provides a corrected scientific implementation and updated reproducibility tools. The principal corrections include: Correcting the colatitude derivative of the associated Legendre functions used in the spherical-harmonic operator. Restoring the radial magnetic-field contribution of the quadratic poloidal Mie term, ensuring consistency with the continuous divergence-free representation. Updating the corresponding current-reconstruction and recoverability calculations. Clarifying the scaled coefficient parameterization, Bayesian prior, and interpretation of coefficient-space resolution diagnostics. Improving numerical verification, reproducibility workflows, and documentation. The updated calculations continue to support the importance of satellite altitude separation for constraining specified ionospheric current structures, while distinguishing formal information gain from recovery of the complete physical current distribution. Data and Reproducibility The package includes source code, documentation, numerical tests, small reference summaries, sample orbit positions, and a self-contained synthetic example. The synthetic demonstrations can be executed without downloading mission magnetic-field observations. Reproducing the study's observation-based analyses requires the corresponding processed Swarm and Macau Science Satellite-1 data and additional external inputs described in the documentation. Large intermediate numerical archives and original magnetic observation records are not redistributed in this software package. Citation and License Please cite the version-specific Zenodo DOI and the software authors listed in CITATION.cff when using this package. Author-owned software and documentation are distributed under the MIT License. Included spacecraft-derived orbit excerpts and external datasets remain subject to their respective data-provider terms. This release supersedes the previous software implementation while retaining earlier versions in the same Zenodo version history.

items.summary: Tabular foundation models (TFMs) are increasingly deployed through black-box APIs and trained on large collections of real-world tabular datasets. As this training paradigm becomes more widely adopted, private or proprietary datasets may be incorporated into pre-training corpora, yet there are currently no dedicated methods for determining whether a given tabular dataset was used to train a TFM. As a solution, we introduce the first dataset inference method for TFMs, aiming to infer whether a suspect dataset was part of a model's pre-training data. We systematically analyze a broad collection of candidate signals that can be observed from a black-box TFM via input manipulation and find that individual signals provide only weak evidence of training data membership. However, by combining multiple complementary signals, we can infer dataset membership for several state-of-the-art TFMs trained on real tabular data, achieving up to 0.99 ROCAUC dependent on the TFM. We then study factors that influence dataset identification, including pre-training data composition, model capacity, and the use of real vs. synthetic data. Our results show that our dataset inference method is a practical auditing tool for detecting privacy leakage and the use of proprietary datasets in TFMs.
items.title: Dataset Inference for Data Provenance and Privacy Auditing in Tabular Foundation Models

items.summary: Absorption and scattering coefficients for the Jerlov optical water types, taken from the primary literature with the provenance of every value recorded. Values that a published table got wrong are flagged rather than silently repaired, and quantities the data do not determine are refused rather than guessed. Twenty-five entries are documented, nine of them confirmed defects in the source literature: duplicated rows in Solonenko & Mobley (2015) Table 7, a transcription error in the small-particle scattering coefficient that propagated into their published coefficients, a Data Availability Statement that gives the DOI of an unrelated dataset, and a reprint whose stated unit is out by a factor of ten. Three further entries were open questions that obtaining the 1968 first edition settled. The same Jerlov water type is in circulation with beam attenuations differing by a factor of five, which is why every coefficient here carries the source it came from. Every shipped table can be regenerated from its primary source by the scripts in tools/ , and each generation step checks the result against the equations of the paper it came from. The package computes the direct and veiling components along a horizontal underwater path, converts spectra to CIE XYZ, sRGB, or the response of an arbitrary camera or set of photoreceptors, gives the Jerlov type that typically applies in each 10 m layer down to 200 m and carries the downwelling irradiance down through those layers, integrates photosynthetically available radiation (PAR), or the photon flux over any other band or weighted by any spectral sensitivity, with depth, gives the spectrum at any depth and the effective Kd between two, and finds the depth at which PAR falls to 1 percent, ranks the Jerlov types by their distance from a measured Kd spectrum, carries Jerlov's measured profiles of quanta irradiance (350-700 nm) by water type and checks the depth profile against them, carries Tyler's (1958) measured radiance distribution in Lake Pend Oreille, carries the wave-induced light fluctuations measured by Darecki et al. (2011) and Gernez & Antoine (2009), read from their figures, carries the Paulson & Simpson (1977) shortwave penetration parameters used by ocean circulation models, converts a backscattering sensor's single-angle reading into the backscattering coefficient, and carries Petzold's (1972) volume scattering functions for eight measured ocean waters.
items.title: jerlov: inherent optical properties of the Jerlov optical water types, with provenance

items.summary: Runtime query similarity identification supports several activities, including workload analysis, identifying recurring behaviour, auditing, debugging, and anomaly detection. Existing methods for evaluating query similarity mostly rely on SQL text, execution plans, or result values but do not account for input data or how results are derived during query execution. This paper proposes a novel approach using data provenance for query-template identification. We construct query-level profiles that capture explicit data dependencies, occurrence frequencies, and structural properties by aggregating tuple-level Lineage and Why-provenance across entire query results. We also derive Provenance Structural Descriptors (PSD), which summarise these profiles using a small set of numerical features. We evaluate our proposals using these profiles to identify query templates over \(12{,}500\) distinct query instances generated from parametrised TPC-DS query templates. The experimental evaluation shows that query templates can be identified solely from their provenance footprints, and that accuracy improves as more historical data becomes available. It also shows that PSD achieve high classification accuracy with limited training history and low test-processing cost.
items.title: Data Provenance Aggregation and Structural Descriptors for Query-Template Identification

items.summary: This deposit contains the model code, the complete parameter set with provenance labels, all numerical outputs, and the scripts required to regenerate every figure and table in the associated manuscript. The work is a physiologically based kinetic (PBK) analysis of the renal exposure window of emodin, an anthraquinone of rhubarb. The model is an eight-compartment, perfusion-limited PBK model with intestinal and hepatic first-pass metabolism, biliary excretion and enterohepatic recirculation, parameterised for mouse, rat and human. No experimental data were generated: the study is entirely computational. The published pharmacokinetic data used for calibration and external validation are cited in the manuscript; the extracted values are recorded in results/validation_split.csv. The absorption term was calibrated against four published rat plasma datasets, and the fitted value with all residuals is included. Code is additionally available under the MIT licence (see LICENSE-CODE.txt); data and figures are released under CC BY 4.0.
items.title: Data and code for: A physiologically based kinetic analysis of the renal exposure window of emodin

We introduce a constraint-aware optimization framework combining Balanced Mean Squared Error, a Siamese anti-symmetric regularizer, and a novel OOD-margin consistency loss on the per-position feature representation, requiring no architectural changes to the SPURS backbone. A controlled diagnostic on Ssym reveals that anti-symmetric training does not eliminate systematic forward-reverse bias, indicating that gains arise through implicit regularization rather than exact thermodynamic constraint enforcement.

items.summary: The manuscript develops a risk-aware operational research framework for strengthening NdFeB permanent-magnet supply-chain resilience under recycling delays, geopolitical disruptions, and uncertain material shortages. It integrates Caputo fractional-order dynamics, delayed recycling flows, strategic procurement and inventory decisions, Pontryagin-type optimality conditions, and Conditional Value-at-Risk (CVaR) within a unified decision model. The study makes three principal contributions. First, it formulates a memory-dependent dynamic model and establishes positivity, boundedness, feasible-region, shortage-free equilibrium, and fractional local-stability results. Second, it incorporates procurement, recycling investment, stock accumulation, and stock release as operational controls and derives the corresponding necessary optimality conditions. Third, it introduces a scenario-based CVaR formulation and compares import-dependent, recycling-oriented, stockpiling-based, and integrated resilience policies under a common non-anticipative framework. In the baseline risk-aware analysis, the recycling-oriented and integrated strategies reduce mean shortage by approximately 74% relative to the import-dependent strategy and decrease the empirical CVaR at the 0.95 level of quadratic shortage loss from approximately 0.921 to 0.067.
items.title: A Caputo Fractional-Order Optimal Control Framework for NdFeB Permanent Magnet Supply-Chain Resilience under Recycling Delay and Geopolitical Risk
